column2: Why does viewing infection as a causal chain matter both for prevention and for interpreting a positive assay?
column3: Disease needs every link from reservoir to host damage, so breaking any link prevents it, and a positive assay is only one element to integrate with exposure, site, host, burden, and timing.

column2: Why is respiratory spread better treated as a particle-size continuum than as two separate categories?
column3: Large wet particles settle quickly while smaller aerosols stay suspended and accumulate in poorly ventilated rooms, so dose depends on distance, time, airflow, activity, masks, filtration, and inactivation.

column3: T-cell deficiency permits opportunistic viruses, fungi, mycobacteria, and protozoa and weakens granulomas, whereas asplenia impairs clearance of opsonised encapsulated organisms and infected erythrocytes.
